news.title: India U15 Football Camp: How AIFF Scouted 12,000 Players for FIFA U-15 World Cup 2026
news.lede: Twelve thousand boys entered the frame. Sixty scouts criss-crossed India for two seasons. They watched school tournaments, youth leagues, national championships, district competitions and open trials. They also tracked Indian footballers growing up in overseas academies.

news.title: India's U15 Football Team Begins Journey to FIFA World Cup 2026
news.lede: The India U15 men's national football squad has commenced its training camp for the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026. Led by head coach Bibiano Fernandes, the camp is underway at the Centre for Sports Excellence in Bengaluru, focusing on readying the team for the esteemed international event. Bibiano Fernandes, who has a rich history with India's youth teams, steps into this role after his appointment was approved by the AIFF Executive Committee. Fernandes is recognized for driving India to the AFC U17 Asian Cup four times and securing multiple SAFF titles, bringing valuable experience to the squad.

news.title: Premier League to adopt major rules seen at 2026 FIFA World Cup: 5-sec countdown, 1-min injury ban and mo
news.lede: The 2026/27 Premier League season will bring several changes to how matches are restarted, substitutions are handled, injured players return to the field and certain red-card decisions are reviewed by VAR. Alongside those mandatory changes to the Laws of the Game, the Premier League has also published its ‘Football Principles’ and ‘Refereeing Points of Emphasis’ for the new campaign, setting out how referees and VAR officials are expected to approach a range of situations. Football News: The Premier League is set to implement significant rule changes for the 2026/27 season, including a five-second countdown for throw-ins, a one-minute injury protocol, and enhanced VAR interventions. These changes aim to reduce time-wasting and improve match efficiency.

(AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez, File) A host of European federations have already scrapped their backing of Infantino, including England, Ireland and Wales. LONDON The Scottish Football Association has withdrawn its support for embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino after his failed attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup. A host of European federations have already scrapped their backing of Infantino, including England, Ireland and Wales.

news.title: Six post-World Cup transfers that caught our eye: Vozinha, Torres, Spence...
news.lede: Four weeks have passed since the World Cup final and plenty of players from the tournament have been making moves since then. It happens every four years. The World Cup is the perfect stage for a player to put themselves in the spotlight and attract new suitors at club level. This summer has been no different, with several protagonists from the World Cup making moves since.

news.title: Chelsea fan displays Falklands flag during match as Argentinian player booed
news.lede: A Chelsea supporter displayed a Falkland Islands flag as Enzo Fernandez came onto the pitch during Saturday's friendly win over Real Sociedad. The Argentine, who replaced Reece James, received a mixed reaction from the Stamford Bridge crowd. Fernandez was part of Argentina's World Cup squad, with the group drawing attention for several references to the Falklands. After their 2-1 semi‑final victory over England, a group of players held up a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' - 'The Falklands are Argentine.'

news.title: The Korean national football team fails to secure a spot in the Round of 32 |
news.lede: The South Korean national football team concluded its journey as they failed to join round of 32 in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada, Mexico, and the United States. Although South Korea awaited the results of other matches after completing their group stage games, they ultimately failed to secure a spot in the knockout stage. During the group stage, South Korea faced a challenging set of matches, losing two games out of three and competing against formidable opponents. Their advancement to the knockout stage depended not only on their own performance in these three matches but also on the outcomes of other games taking place across different groups.
